account: Today appears to be an ordinary working day, with no confirmed emergency or unusual municipal expenditure. During my market walk, the baker's distant shout caught my attention, but he explained that he was advertising fresh bread. He reported eight emeralds in sales and a well-stocked stall, and asked whether town gatherings would need bread. I have not confirmed any orders. During the scheduled town accounts appointment, I counted 128 emeralds in the treasury and left them untouched. The secretary reported no outstanding bills or confirmed delivery assignments. Freight repeatedly offered warehouse deliveries and a ferry ride to my tea appointment; I told him there were no confirmed deliveries and chose to walk across the bridge. These offers seem to concern his usual business, not an established town project. The builder has called out several times, but I have not understood his words, so I cannot say whether anything urgent prompted them. The secretary says his repair-quote appointment is at 16:30 in my office, and I intend to hear the proposal then rather than assume its purpose. The secretary also confirmed my tea venue and handed me a book titled 'Tea venue confirmed,' which I have not yet read. I reached the neighbour's east-dock cottage just before three. The neighbour welcomed me for our usual tea and asked about my day. I have asked for dockside news but have not yet heard any. After tea I must return to the office for 16:30.
